newsitem.title: USA: FAA probes near-collision of planes in California.
newsitem.headline: FAA probes near-collision of planes in California.

text.p: The Federal Aviation Administration launched an investigation into the near-collision of a Reno Air passenger jet and a private plane in San Jose, California, a spokesman said Friday.
"We are looking to determine what precisely occurred," said FAA spokesman Mitch Barker.

The airplanes were taking off early Thursday from the San Jose International Airport, 40 miles south of San Francisco, on parallel runways when the private Cessna 172 turned into the path of the Reno Air MD83 jetliner.
The Reno Air jet, carrying 111 passengers and five crew members, took evasive action to avert a collision with the small private plane, Reno Air spokesman Steve Sarner said.
Sarner said the airline had not determined how close the two planes came to colliding. But according to local news reports they came to within 100 to 200 feet of each other.
The Reno Air jet, on route to Las Vegas, continued to its destination without further incident, the airline said. There were no injuries.
